children: , the NAND flash and enterprise storage company, drew a Buy rating and a $2,400 price target from Rosenblatt as the firm made the case that AI demand could lift the value of its storage products. Shares fell about 2% to $1,849.38 Wednesday morning, leaving the target roughly 29.8% above that price.

The business has given bulls something concrete to point to. Sandisk reported $8.97 billion in fiscal fourth-quarter revenue, up 51% from the prior quarter. Enterprise storage is central to the growth case, but an analyst target still depends on Sandisk turning demand into durable margins.

The picture adds a useful check on the excitement: Sandisk's GF Score is 51 out of 100. Growth and financial strength appear stronger than its value and momentum readings. That gap is the investor question now. Can Sandisk keep improving its business fast enough to justify the price investors are paying for it?

title: Sandisk Falls 3.2% While $2,400 Target Tests AI Storage Faith
